cause: Each guard was added to protect claim authority - never reap an orchestrator claim, require a CAS revision, require a scope binding, one active claim per task and per task set - but none of them shipped with a matching exit. Guards compose into a closed set: every new precondition removes states from the reachable graph, and with no recovery command the intersection eventually becomes empty. The reaper made this invisible by reporting a dead orchestrator claim with the same reason string as a healthy one.
prevention: Ship an exit with every guard. Concretely: owner-bound adopt supplies the fields a legacy claim is missing so heartbeat and renew can reach it again; owner-bound terminalize ends a provably dead claim regardless of mode without deleting, releasing, or completing it; activate-store makes a fresh checkout usable without a consumer agent_runtime.yml. Both mutating commands refuse an unidentified caller, require a reason, record owner identity and before/after sha256, and terminalize refuses a live claim. claim_reaper now evaluates liveness before the orchestrator branch and lists a dead orchestrator claim under needs_owner_recovery naming the exact command, so the state is never silent again.
summary: A fourth recurrence in the claim-authority family, this time fatal: an expired claim stayed status=claimed and was reachable by no registered command at all. The reaper skipped it on mode before testing liveness, heartbeat and renew rejected it for predating mutation_revision/scope_binding, task and task-set exclusivity refused any replacement claim, and no expire/terminalize/bootstrap subcommand existed. One stale claim blocked both its own task and the recovery task needed to fix it, so the only exit was an Owner-authorized manual JSON mutation.
title: Give every claim state a registered exit before adding guards
